A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PIGDreamer work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Safety-Gymnasium experiments, component ablations, a privileged-agent case study, and training-time measurements in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Guard results and an imagination-procedure comparison. The model-free baseline scores are explicitly attributed to SafePO, but other reported outcomes are produced by this work.

M1.justification: The dual world models, oracle representation alignment, privileged predictors and critics, Twisted Imagination, and augmented-Lagrangian objective remain unchanged. Nested Latent Imagination appears only as an added ablation comparator.

E1.justification: v2 adds Guard evaluations on GoalAnt8Hazards, GoalAnt8Ghosts, and GoalHumanoid8Hazards, extending coverage to Ant and Humanoid agents and additional obstacle environments. The five original Safety-Gymnasium tasks remain; the model-free and NLI comparisons reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds numerical comparisons against CPO, FOCOPS, PPO Lag, and TRPO Lag, which v1 described without reporting corresponding results; their scores are imported from SafePO. Table 1 additionally evaluates NLI. Distill already appeared in v1 Table 6, retained as v2 Table 9.

E3.justification: The stated 64×64 observations, 4M environment steps, and ten 1,000-step evaluation episodes remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce a TI-versus-NLI control and a model-free comparison using baseline cost limits of 25 versus PIGDreamer's 2. Guard performance is aggregated across three tasks.

E4.justification: v2 adds a three-task ablation comparing Twisted Imagination with Nested Latent Imagination (Table 1), testing the trajectory-generation choice. Results show mixed reward and cost advantages. The original representation/critic ablations and PointButton1 privileged-agent case study remain.

E5.justification: The unchanged aggregate ablation plot loses its explicit five-runs-per-task statement when v1 Figure 6 becomes v2 Figure 7. The three-run, 95% bootstrap-CI description remains for the main Safety-Gymnasium aggregate. New Table 7 uses ± values without defining the statistic or run count; these edits do not establish changed execution counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds Guard, model-free, and NLI/TI result entries. Guard Table 6 reports average reward/cost of 10.68/4.59 for PIGDreamer versus 4.52/4.24 for SafeDreamer, with training times of 19.14 versus 14.97 hours. The resulting approximately 28% time overhead concerns Guard; the original Safety-Gymnasium 22.4% overhead and Distill comparison values remain in Tables 8–9.

T1.justification: The ACPOMDP definitions, Lemmas 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3, Appendix A proof, and Appendix C derivation are unchanged. Equations 9 and 10 exchange order without changing their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central ACPOMDP and PIGDreamer contributions remain. v2 explicitly adds robustness to the abstract's claims, broadens the claimed empirical scope beyond Safety-Gymnasium and model-based comparisons, and highlights a 136% reward improvement with 28% additional training time from Guard.

C2.justification: v2 adds an information-gap explanation for privileged methods' failures on Guard, argues that TI's lighter design supports robustness and versatility, and attributes model-free deficits partly to missing history and privileged information. The existing PointButton1 limitation and call for task-specific privileged-information research remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, identifies SafePO as the source of model-free baseline scores, and supplies Guard training-time measurements. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware specifications, and privileged-information descriptions are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Avalos et al. (2024) on learned belief updates and Zhao et al. (2024) for Guard, with a limited extension of the robustness positioning. The two Ji 2023 entries refer to the same previously cited Safety-Gymnasium work.

P1.justification: v2 tightens wording and terminology, revises the experimental discussion into 'Benchmarking Privileged Variants,' corrects Figure 4.2 references to Figure 3, and adds Appendix D.4 on model-free comparisons. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation expands substantially: Figure 4 becomes a two-benchmark composite, Figure 5 adds a Guard training-time chart, and Tables 1, 6, and 7 introduce three new comparisons. Retained diagrams and plots are resized or relocated, including separating Figures 2 and 3 onto different pages.

improvement.justification: Guard extends the evidence beyond the original robot families, while the NLI ablation tests a previously untested design choice; the code link also improves access information. These are useful gains, tempered by unclear uncertainty reporting for the new studies and unequal cost limits in the model-free comparison. Broad safety claims also exceed the Guard evidence: PIGDreamer's average cost is 4.59 versus SafeDreamer's 4.24. Overall empirical support improves modestly.
